title: Fit a cable through a cable gland and tighten it snug
instruction: Fit the cable through the cable gland into the box until its sheath reaches at least 5 mm past the gland's inner end, then tighten the cap nut snug, between the marks, neither short of them nor past them. Then let go of both.
context: Electricians fit a cable gland wherever a cable enters an enclosure: tightened right, it seals the box against water and dust and anchors the cable; too loose it lets the cable pull out, too tight it crushes the sheath.
setup: All positions from the arm bases' midline (x forward, y left). Fixed on the table: a grey polycarbonate enclosure, 120 mm deep x 160 mm wide x 60 mm tall, 3 mm walls, lid off, its near wall's outer face at x 0.27 m, centred on the midline. In the middle of the near wall, its axis along x and 35 mm above the table: an M20 x 1.5 black-grey polyamide cable gland (for real trials: any EN 62444 M20 x 1.5 polyamide IP68 gland with a seal for 8 mm) (22 mm hex flange outside, 24 mm locknut inside, rubber seal insert open to 14.5 mm, domed cap nut 24 mm across flats with a 13 mm mouth); the cap nut starts loose, on the thread's first turn. On the table: a round control cable, 3 cores x 1.5 mm2, grey PVC sheath 8 mm across (real trials: H05VV-F 3G1.5, EN 50525-2-11) (~100 g/m), 420 mm of sheath from a fixed black plastic cable clamp (24 x 22 x 18 mm) at x 0.10 m, y -0.24 m (cable leaving it 30 degrees left of x), then its prepared end: sheath stripped back 75 mm, the three cores (brown, blue, green-yellow) taped together. The cable lies in an arc, its sheath's cut end at x 0.16 m, y 0.08 m, the cores pointing toward the box (tip ~4 cm in front of the wall, ~4 cm left of the gland's axis). The cap nut tightens clockwise as seen from the arms; 3 turns bring the seal onto the cable.
scoring: Marks: turns of the cap nut from first contact C (the seal gripping the cable all round), set by a calibration of the hardware described in the README: H = first 1/8-turn step where the cable holds a 30 N pull (EN 62444 anchorage), T = the cap-nut torque (3 Nm), D = first step with sheath or seal damage. Measured on the specified gland and cable, and used in the simulation: H 1, T 1.5, D 1.75 turns. Sheath past = the cable runs through the gland and its sheath's cut end is at least 5 mm past the gland's inner end. Pull test = hands off 1 s, then 30 N outward (ramped 1 s, held 0.5 s); holds if the sheath moves under 2 mm. 1.0 (success) = sheath past, holds, nut between H and T, still 1 s; 0.75 = sheath past, holds, past T (over-tightened); 0.5 = sheath past, holds, short of H; 0.25 = sheath past only; 0 = otherwise, or the nut ever at D or beyond (crushed).
reset_notes: Unscrew the cap nut to the thread's first turn (seal open, 3 turns before it touches the cable), pull the cable out and lay it back in its arc as in the screenshot. A crushed sheath must be replaced (cut and strip a fresh end).
fidelity: CPU PhysX 240 Hz. Own simplified parts, no third-party CAD (M20 x 1.5 per ISO 261). Cap nut on a jointed thread (1.5 mm/turn, constant 0.08 Nm friction); seal = 6 rubber pads on springs, grip from contact friction. Cable = chain of 20 mm links with springs and a creeping set. No torque or sheath-damage model: marks H, T, D measured on real hardware (README). Pull test applied by the task.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; scripted demo: 1.0 (success at step 3,480); over-tightened: 0.75; holds but short of the marks: 0.5; pushed through, not tightened: 0.25; crushed: 0.0
